structure.title: Separate tales
structure.text: Each story establishes its own family, danger, and rules. The collection does not require a continuous cast or a single plot.

structure.title: Repeated patterns
structure.text: Promises, transformations, sibling contrasts, and improbable helpers recur with variations. Comparing them reveals different uses of familiar story machinery.

people.name: The youngest child
people.text: The third son or youngest daughter, mocked as simple by older siblings, who so often turns out to be the one who succeeds.

people.name: The stranger or helper
people.text: An old woman, a dwarf or a talking animal met on the road, whose request for kindness quietly decides how the hero's journey will go.

people.name: The bargain
people.text: A promise made too lightly, to a frog, a witch or a little man, whose price comes due later and is rarely what the speaker expected.

context.title: Tale logic
context.text: Magic usually has consequences within a story's stated conditions. Taking a small instruction seriously may matter more than physical strength.

context.title: A selected collection
context.text: Editions differ in selection and wording. This primer describes recurring features without assuming every familiar Grimm tale is included.
context.takeaway: Let the actual contents guide comparison.

notice.text: Notice repeated trials with one altered detail.
notice.why: Repetition teaches the reader how to recognise the decisive difference.

notice.text: Follow exchanges of food and shelter.
notice.why: Everyday generosity can have extraordinary consequences.

opening: Children are sent into forests, bargains are made with strangers, and a hungry household can become more frightening than the creatures outside it. In the Grimms' tales, danger arrives quickly and survival often depends on noticing a rule, keeping a promise, or accepting help from something easily overlooked. The stories move with a blunt confidence that makes their wonders feel ordinary. A few pages can hold abandonment, terror, ingenuity, and a reversal of fortune extravagant enough to answer a wish everyday life would scarcely permit.
